subject.title: fix(line): dripping inbound media downloads hang past setup timeout

question: Should LINE inbound media use an unconditional 120-second response-body wall-clock, accepting that slower valid transfers will be rejected?
rationale: The code can enforce the proposed deadline, but source inspection and loopback tests cannot determine the intended user-facing cutoff for real LINE CDN transfers.

options.title: Confirm 120 seconds and prove it
options.body: Approve the Slack/Feishu-aligned cutoff and require redacted live LINE evidence for a delayed or representative large-media download plus the timeout failure path.

options.title: Choose a different bounded policy
options.body: Replace the fixed value with an owner-approved longer or throughput-aware bound and add focused success and timeout coverage for that contract.

options.title: Accept the cutoff explicitly
options.body: Merge the current policy while explicitly owning the possibility that valid transfers lasting over 120 seconds will surface as unavailable media.

recommendation.title: Confirm 120 seconds and prove it
recommendation.body: Approve the Slack/Feishu-aligned cutoff and require redacted live LINE evidence for a delayed or representative large-media download plus the timeout failure path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the current LINE download and cancellation contract, making them the strongest history-backed routing candidate for this timeout decision.
